schema_note: Fixture allowlist for the synthtwin data-provenance guard (plan D13). Each entry in 'fixtures' binds one committed data fixture to its origin and must contain exactly these keys: 'path' (repository-relative POSIX path of the committed fixture file), 'generator' (repository-relative path of the seeded script that rebuilds the fixture; invoked as: python <generator> --seed <seed> --out <output-path>), 'seed' (integer seed; the same seed must always produce the same bytes on every platform), 'sha256' (64-character lowercase hex digest of the committed fixture bytes), and 'justification' (a written sentence explaining why this fixture must be committed instead of being built at test time). The checker tools/provenance/check_provenance.py re-runs every generator and byte-compares its output to the committed file; any difference fails. Both 'path' and 'generator' must be repository-relative (no absolute paths, no '..' components), must stay inside the repository, and must be tracked by git once the repository has commits. Generators are executed through tools/provenance/guard_runner.py, which installs a Python audit hook before the generator code runs; the hook refuses imports of network, process, and native-capability modules and blocks the known socket, process-creation, and native-call audit events. That runner is a best-effort in-process guard, not a sandbox or a confinement mechanism: repository source review of every generator script and the CI checks are the operative controls (CI is the authoritative automated verification; while the repository is private no branch ruleset is applied, so it is a standing rule rather than a mechanically enforced merge barrier). JSON is treated as a data format: a tracked .json file is allowed only if it is one of the checker's known configuration files (KNOWN_CONFIG_JSON in the checker) or listed here. Committed fixtures must be tiny (at most 100000 bytes). Phase 1 commits exactly one: the numeric reference vectors, which are mathematics rather than data - they contain no value taken from any table, and their generator imports none of the code they check.

fixtures.justification: Reference values for the profiler's mean, standard deviation, skewness and percentile ladder, computed by exact rational arithmetic. They are committed rather than built at test time because their whole purpose is to be an oracle the implementation cannot influence: a value recomputed beside the code it checks could drift with it, and round 1 of the Phase 1 review found exactly that defect in the golden hash. The generator imports only fractions, decimal, json, math and struct - never synthtwin, never numpy, never pandas - and every float64 it reports is proved correctly rounded by exact integer comparison against the midpoints to its neighbours. No value in this file comes from any real or synthetic table.
